coverageNote: Method-selection skill: 12 structural types (identify-rule, the four single-rule select-and-apply shapes, the area rule, three two-step chains, and three bearings shapes). Type coverage wins over the 8-10 quiz ceiling, so the quiz runs to 12 items, one per type.

options.why: The sine rule needs a complete opposite pair; here only two sides and the included angle are known, not a side with its opposite angle.
The area rule finds an area from two sides and their included angle, not the length of the third side.
Pythagoras' theorem needs a right angle, but this triangle has none.

questions.solution_text: Two sides ($12$ cm and $7$ cm) and the included angle ($40^{\circ}$) are known and $x$ is the third side, which is the **cosine rule**.

options.why: Used Pythagoras ($\sqrt{9^{2}+13^{2}}$), ignoring the $-2ab\cos C$ term of the cosine rule.
Added $2ab\cos C$ instead of subtracting it.
Used $\sin 58^{\circ}$ in place of $\cos 58^{\circ}$ in the cosine rule.

questions.solution_text:
Two sides and the included angle, so use the **cosine rule**.
$x^{2}=9^{2}+13^{2}-2(9)(13)\cos 58^{\circ}$
$x=\sqrt{250-234\cos 58^{\circ}}$
$=11.2249\ldots$
$\approx 11.2$ cm

options.why: Put the known angle on top: multiplied by $\sin 72^{\circ}$ and divided by $\sin 40^{\circ}$.
Used the third angle $68^{\circ}$ instead of the $40^{\circ}$ opposite $x$.

questions.solution_text:
A side ($15$ m) and its opposite angle ($72^{\circ}$) are a complete pair, so use the **sine rule**.
$\dfrac{x}{\sin 40^{\circ}}=\dfrac{15}{\sin 72^{\circ}}$
$x=\dfrac{15\sin 40^{\circ}}{\sin 72^{\circ}}$
$=10.138\ldots$
$\approx 10.1$ m

options.why: Dropped the negative sign of $\cos\theta$, giving the acute supplement instead of the obtuse angle.
Placed the wrong side ($6$) opposite $\theta$ in the cosine rule instead of the $13$.

questions.solution_text:
All three sides, so use the **cosine rule** for an angle with the side opposite $\theta$ (the $13$) as $c$.
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{6^{2}+10^{2}-13^{2}}{2(6)(10)}$
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{-33}{120}$
$\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{-33}{120}\right)$
$=105.9\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 106^{\circ}$

options.why: Took the obtuse supplement when the angle is acute.
Found the third angle rather than the one opposite the $8$ side.

questions.solution_text:
A side ($11$) and its opposite angle ($64^{\circ}$) are a complete pair, so use the **sine rule** with $\sin$ on top; $\theta$ is opposite the $8$.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{8}=\dfrac{\sin 64^{\circ}}{11}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{8\sin 64^{\circ}}{11}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8\sin 64^{\circ}}{11}\right)$
$=40.8188\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 40.8^{\circ}$

options.why: Omitted the factor of $\tfrac{1}{2}$ in the area rule.
Used $\cos 52^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 52^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
Two sides and the included angle, so use the **area rule**.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$
$=\dfrac{1}{2}(18)(11)\sin 52^{\circ}$
$\approx 78.0\text{ cm}^{2}$

options.why: Found the angle opposite the $20$ side instead of $\angle A$, which is opposite the $14$ side.
Took the obtuse supplement of the correct acute angle.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
Two sides and the included angle give $AC$ by the **cosine rule**.
$AC^{2}=20^{2}+14^{2}-2(20)(14)\cos 63^{\circ}$
$AC=\sqrt{596-560\cos 63^{\circ}}$
$=18.486\ldots$ cm
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
The **sine rule** gives $\angle A$, opposite $BC=14$.
$\dfrac{\sin A}{14}=\dfrac{\sin 63^{\circ}}{18.486\ldots}$
$A=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{14\sin 63^{\circ}}{18.486\ldots}\right)$
$\approx 42^{\circ}$

options.why: Omitted the $\tfrac{1}{2}$ factor when applying the area rule.
Multiplied the wrong pair of sides — the found angle sits between the $9$ and $13$ sides, not the $9$ and $17$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
The area rule needs an angle. With three sides, find $\angle C$ (between the $9$ and $13$ sides, opposite the $17$) by the **cosine rule**.
$\cos C=\dfrac{9^{2}+13^{2}-17^{2}}{2(9)(13)}$
$C=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{-39}{234}\right)=99.594\ldots^{\circ}$
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}(9)(13)\sin 99.594\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 57.7\text{ cm}^{2}$

options.why: Omitted the $\tfrac{1}{2}$ factor in the area rule.
Used $70^{\circ}$ as the included angle instead of the $50^{\circ}$ between the two known sides at $A$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
The area rule needs two sides and their included angle; only $AB$ is known. $\angle C=180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-70^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$, and $AC$ (opposite $\angle B$) comes from the **sine rule**.
$AC=\dfrac{45\sin 70^{\circ}}{\sin 60^{\circ}}=48.83\ldots\text{ m}$
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
Sides $AB=45$ and $AC=48.83\ldots$ meet at $\angle A=50^{\circ}$.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}(45)(48.83\ldots)\sin 50^{\circ}$
$\approx 842\text{ m}^{2}$

options.why: Subtracted the bearings ($140^{\circ}-55^{\circ}$) instead of using the back bearing to get the $95^{\circ}$ included angle.
Used Pythagoras, ignoring the included angle altogether.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
Back bearing of $P$ from $Q$ is $055^{\circ}+180^{\circ}=235^{\circ}$, and $R$ is on $140^{\circ}$:
$\angle PQR=235^{\circ}-140^{\circ}=95^{\circ}$.
2. **Apply the rule to find the first unknown**
$PR^{2}=80^{2}+110^{2}-2(80)(110)\cos 95^{\circ}$
$PR=\sqrt{18500-17600\cos 95^{\circ}}$
$=141.54\ldots$
$\approx 142$ km

options.why: Omitted the $\tfrac{1}{2}$ factor in the area rule.
Used $\cos 85^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 85^{\circ}$ in the area rule.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
Both bearings are from $O$, so the included angle is
$\angle AOB=125^{\circ}-40^{\circ}=85^{\circ}$.
2. **Apply the rule to find the first unknown**
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}(18)(26)\sin 85^{\circ}$
$\approx 233.1\text{ km}^{2}$

options.why: Added $\angle ACB$ to the bearing of $B$ from $C$ instead of subtracting it.
Used the forward bearing $122^{\circ}$ instead of its back bearing $302^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
The bearing of $B$ from $C$ is the back bearing of $122^{\circ}$: $122^{\circ}+180^{\circ}=302^{\circ}$.
$A$ lies $\angle ACB\approx 29.7^{\circ}$ anticlockwise of $CB$, so the bearing of $A$ from $C$ is
$302^{\circ}-29.7^{\circ}$
$\approx 272^{\circ}\text{T}$
